aspects.says: A participant test that builds its Context by hand can share the participant's wrong key; a Context from a real IncomingListener has the keys production uses.
basis: section:11.1 A Participant Test Gets Its Context From `IncomingListener`

aspects.says: A test that calls commit or abort by hand checks its author's idea of the TransactionManager; the vote decides who hears the outcome, so the whole vote is asserted and the abort path is tested through the real TransactionManager.
basis: section:11.2 Only the Real TransactionManager Decides Who Hears the Outcome

aspects.says: Tests that share a Q2 share its participants, the objects they found by name, the Space and the NameRegistrar, so each test brings its own data, and registering a new object does not reach a participant that already holds the old one.
basis: section:11.3 Tests That Share a Q2 Share Its State

aspects.says: Only a socket test on the shipped descriptors, with a client built from the network's specification, tests the server's port, channel and packager; a client copied from the descriptor agrees with it whatever it says.
basis: section:11.4 Only a Socket Test With the Terminals' Framing Tests `50_server.xml`

aspects.says: State shared between sessions shows only when two transactions are in the participant at once, which a test forces by holding one inside a stand-in it controls; requests sent one after another never overlap.
basis: section:11.5 Only Two Transactions in Flight Show What Sessions Share
